_doc: DECLARED DISCONTINUITIES IN THE SYSTEM'S OWN SERIES.
Rule 1.3 (PROGRESS/CORTEX++_TASKS_2026-08-20.txt): 'Ako teglata mrudnat —
seriite se markirat kato prekusnati, ne mulchalivo.' If the weights move, the
series are marked BROKEN, not silently continued.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A COMMENT. goal_score_calculator already refuses to compare
two composites with different config_fingerprint values — that is the mechanical
half. This file is the HUMAN-READABLE half: which break, when, why, and what it
measurably did to the numbers. A fingerprint that changed with no record beside
it tells a later reader that the series broke but not what broke it.
TWO KINDS OF BREAK, and `break_kind` says which — added 18 Sep 2026 after the
five records of 17 Sep were written with no fingerprints at all, because the
only field for saying what changed could not express what had changed.
break_kind = 'tree'        the goal tree moved: an axis entered or left, or a
weight or kind changed. config_fingerprint DIFFERS
across the break, and the mechanical half of the
guard already refuses the comparison.
break_kind = 'instrument'  the tree is byte-identical and the SERIES BEHIND AN
AXIS changed: a different World Bank indicator, a
different definition, a relabelled line.
config_fingerprint is IDENTICAL on both sides —
it hashes axis|weight|kind and is blind to which
series feeds an axis — so the mechanical half does
NOT catch this kind, and instrument_before /
instrument_after carry what moved.
AN INSTRUMENT BREAK IS THE MORE DANGEROUS OF THE TWO, precisely because the
fingerprint keeps saying the two points are comparable. Nothing in the code
refuses it. This file is the only record that they are not.
Every entry states the fingerprint on both sides AND what changed: a different
fingerprint for a tree break, a named instrument pair for an instrument break.
A record that names neither says nothing broke, and the contract test rejects
it. Anything comparing points across a break must say so out loud or refuse.

breaks.cause: GENERAL_SELF_REVIEW retired from the goal tree (config/target_config.json)
breaks.why: Self-observation is a SENSE, not a state of the world. An axis that scores the observer puts the observer inside the observed: a system with degraded sensors could raise its own composite by rating itself higher. The observation continues in core/self_mirror.py and enters no number.

measured_effect.how: goal_score_calculator.compute_goal_score() run twice on the SAME live trends/observations, once against each config. No file was written.
measured_effect.note: composite_score did NOT move: GENERAL_SELF_REVIEW was a semantic axis with no primary_metric, so it was never in the numerator. What moved is the DENOMINATOR of the goal — 6 of the 59 weight that had no live source left the tree, so coverage_of_goal rose from 57.8% to 59.9% WITHOUT a single new measurement. That rise is bookkeeping, not progress, and it is exactly why the break has to be declared: a reader of the coverage series who does not know about this entry would read +2.1 points as a sensor that came online.

breaks.cause: ENERGY_REVIEW anchor and obs key moved from World Bank EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS (renewable share of ELECTRICITY) to EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS (renewable share of TOTAL FINAL ENERGY)
breaks.why: target_config has always declared this axis's primary_metric as renewable_energy_pct with unit 'percent of total energy', and its rationale cites the IEA Net Zero 80% target, which the IEA states for total final energy. The number being scored was the electricity share: a different and larger quantity. Points before and after this date are not comparable — the series did not move, the instrument did.
breaks.measured_effect: World Bank WLD, verified against the live API on 17 Sep 2026: EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS latest 27.8357; EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS 2020 = 19.7355641050053. higher_better against target 80: score 34.8 -> 24.7, a fall of 10.1 points. The axis did not get worse; it stopped being measured by the wrong instrument.
breaks.note: EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS latest available year is 2020 against 2024 for the electricity series. The declared metric with a four-year lag is preferred over a different metric that is current: an axis measured on the wrong quantity cannot be made right by being fresh.
breaks.instrument_before: World Bank EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS (renewable share of ELECTRICITY)
breaks.instrument_after: World Bank EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS (renewable share of TOTAL FINAL ENERGY)
breaks.fingerprint_note: IDENTICAL ON PURPOSE, and this is the point of break_kind. config_fingerprint hashes axis|weight|kind only (goal_score_calculator.config_fingerprint) — it is deliberately blind to WHICH series feeds an axis. This break moved the instrument and not one axis, weight or kind, so the fingerprint cannot and should not differ. What changed is named in instrument_before/instrument_after instead.

breaks.cause: FOOD_REVIEW anchor and obs key moved from SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS (prevalence of undernourishment, PoU) to SN.ITK.SVFI.ZS (FIES prevalence of severe food insecurity)
breaks.why: target_config declares food_insecurity_pct and its rationale cites '~10% severely food insecure' against a target of 2.5. PoU measures whether the dietary energy supply is adequate; FIES measures whether people report going without food. They are different instruments with different values and the axis was scored on the one it does not name.
breaks.measured_effect: World Bank WLD, verified against the live API on 17 Sep 2026: SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS snapshot value 8.5; SN.ITK.SVFI.ZS 2024 = 10.1426518. lower_better against target 2.5: score 29.4 -> 24.6, a fall of 4.8 points.
breaks.instrument_before: World Bank SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS (FAO prevalence of undernourishment)
breaks.instrument_after: World Bank SN.ITK.SVFI.ZS (FAO FIES prevalence of severe food insecurity)

This break moved the instrument and not one axis, weight or kind, so the fingerprint cannot and should not differ. What changed is named in instrument_before/instrument_after instead.

breaks.cause: HUMAN_WELL_BEING_REVIEW anchor and obs key moved from SP.DYN.IMRT.IN (infant mortality, deaths before age 1) to SH.DYN.MORT (under-5 mortality)
breaks.why: target_config declares child_mortality_per_1000 with unit 'deaths per 1000 live births' and target 25, citing SDG 3.2, whose official target is under-5 mortality <=25 by 2030. Infant mortality counts a strict SUBSET of under-5 deaths, so it is always the smaller number. Scoring the subset against the superset's target made the axis look closer to the goal than it is.
breaks.measured_effect: World Bank WLD, verified against the live API on 17 Sep 2026: SP.DYN.IMRT.IN snapshot value 27.7; SH.DYN.MORT 2024 = 37.4 (2023 = 38.3, 2022 = 40). lower_better against target 25: score 90.3 -> 66.8, a fall of 23.4 points.
breaks.over_twenty_points: Yes, and the size is the defect rather than a surprise: under-5 mortality exceeds infant mortality by construction — it counts the same deaths plus every death between ages one and five. 37.4 against 27.7 is that gap, roughly 35% more deaths, and the axis had been graded against the smaller count while claiming the SDG 3.2 target. Nothing about child survival changed on 17 Sep 2026; the axis stopped being scored against an easier number than the one it declares.
breaks.instrument_before: World Bank SP.DYN.IMRT.IN (infant mortality, deaths before age 1)
breaks.instrument_after: UN SDG SH_DYN_MORT (under-5 mortality, UN IGME)

breaks.cause: COGNITION_LEARNING_REVIEW anchor and obs key moved from SE.ADT.LITR.ZS (adult literacy, 15+) to SE.ADT.1524.LT.ZS (youth literacy, 15-24)
breaks.why: target_config declares literacy_rate_youth_pct. Adult literacy includes every cohort schooled in the last sixty years and improves largely as older cohorts age out; youth literacy answers whether education is reaching people now, which is what this axis is about.
breaks.measured_effect: World Bank WLD, verified against the live API on 17 Sep 2026: SE.ADT.LITR.ZS snapshot value 87.74; SE.ADT.1524.LT.ZS 2024 = 93.1100006103516. higher_better against target 100: score 87.7 -> 93.1, a rise of 5.4 points.
breaks.note: This is the one correction of the six that moves an axis UP. It was applied on the same rule as the others — the signed target is the authority — and not because of which way the number went.

breaks.cause: The stored field poverty_190_pct was renamed to poverty_intl_line_pct, and the axis's unit corrected from '$2.15/day' to '$3.00/day (2021 PPP)', to match what World Bank SI.POV.DDAY actually returns.
breaks.why: THE BREAK WAS NOT MADE TODAY — it was made by the World Bank and went unrecorded. The international poverty line moved $1.90 (2011 PPP) -> $2.15 (2017 PPP) -> $3.00 (2021 PPP), and SI.POV.DDAY silently began returning the new series. The World Bank's own indicator note reads: 'As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions.' Points in this axis's history straddle at least one PPP revision and are not comparable, whatever the field was called.
breaks.measured_effect: NONE TODAY. The value is unchanged at 10.4 (2024) and the score is unchanged: lower_better, target 0.0, reference_worst 60.0, 1 - 10.4/60 = 0.8267 -> 82.7. This entry records a discontinuity that already happened upstream and had no entry.
breaks.note: The new field name deliberately does not carry a dollar amount. Encoding the line in the key is what let the name drift two revisions away from the data.
